interactions.title: The Guild’s merfolk-jade vision
lines: DM: As you glance around, you recall what you know about this fourth piece of jade that you're seeking from the Philosopher’s Guild. You remember the message in the letter about this particular piece of jade: “A glittering green thing, smooth jade, sparkling on the brow of a merfolk. The merfolk swims and takes and reaps. The merfolk gloats over the waves of the Elemental Sea, the echoes of Water Eternal. The merfolk commands, the jade resists, but is overwhelmed. The merfolk is a merfolk at peace among kelp forests, singing to the jade, watching the light change through the vast undersea forests. The merfolk is a merfolk slaughtering, taking the jade.”

before: Kenzo: Fucking great.
DM: Okay. Enough.
Seeker: Thank you. Close that.

DM: So we begin. As Seeker finishes his teleport spell, and the cold of Ursk fades around you in an instant as you’re pulled through space. The first thing you notice is the heat, the jarring shift from the cold north, where the beginning of May is barely the beginning of spring to the warmth of the Gulf of Chardon, where it feels practically summer.
DM: The second thing you notice is the darkness: from morning light in Ursk to the pre-dawn inky blackness, only a thin crescent moon casting a faint light on the water.
after: DM: You also recall the story you learned from Thomas Hawke in—in Tollen, who you talk to at a Pyravela party, and he told you the story he had heard from the West, the inspiration for one of his plays.

DM: The play itself, Luminastra’s Gift, is the story of a magic whale who rescues a sailor and takes him to a strange world beneath the ocean. But the inspiration supposedly was a real story that Tom has heard secondhand, a tale from the oceans west of Chardon, of the provinces across the Gulf of Chardon from the great city itself. So that’s on this peninsula where you’ve teleported. It was a tale of a magical kelp forest of jade beneath the ocean, which was tended by merfolk, who grew names in their gardens.

DM: As you recall these stories in these little tiny scraps of information, that is all you have to go on as you search for a piece of jade in a vast— the vast western oceans. You look around and you see you’re on the docks of a city, the city Nevium, the provincial capital of Portalia, a province in the Chardonian Empire.

DM: This is the city that you docked at after you left the canal when you traveled through a year—almost a year ago now, and it’s the closest point to the canal where Seeker had ever seen, because, as you recall, you all traveled through the canal in the mirror, except for Wellby. So the closest to the canal you could reasonably teleport right now. Everything is dark and quiet. The air smells of fish and damp wood, the morning silence broken by the creak of ships at dock and ships anchored out to sea in the harbor. The city itself is built over the ocean, mostly over marsh—tidal marshes, it seems—on great wooden pilings. And they—so—
Delwath: We have the—

interactions.title: Kenzo develops a sense for the missing jade
lines: Kenzo: Yeah, so basically, Tim, I, I spend the—like, as soon as we get the jade, basically, Kenzo is just like—like attuning to the jade. Like, he’s just like, you know, there’s a new piece.

Kenzo: Yeah, Tim, you know, now that there’s like 3 pieces together, 2 more missing, you know, Kenzo spends just like kind of all of his time, like yelling through— get this, this jade connection, and also kind of again searching for the missing one. It’s almost like, you know, trying to like— you know, see if he can feel where or sense through, like, where the missing pieces, if he can kinda get a feeling of it’s, it’s, it’s energy, or it’s, it’s—

DM: Okay. So you— if you are close, like, if it was within a few miles of you, like, I forget what I said the range of your, like, Sense Nature. It’s like 6 miles or— yeah, 10 miles. Something like that.
DM: You're pretty sure that you'd be able to sense its presence with that ability, but not from hundreds of miles away.
Kenzo: Perfect. So Kenzo spends the time to develop that sense.
Kenzo: Further developed in a sense.

before: Kenzo: Hey, Tim, how long has it been since we got the last piece of jade?
Seeker: We just got it, didn't we?
DM: Yeah. Like.
Seeker: And how are the—
DM: No, last night— yesterday afternoon.
after: Delwath: We have no— oh, sorry! Go ahead.
Riswynn: I was just going to say Riswynn has a developed sense of preservation, and thinks we should casually walk away from the Chardonian guard, since we’re probably Chardon’s most wanted.
Delwath: As I say, we have no actual plan here, right?
Riswynn: Try to make—
DM: Literally, no.

interactions.title: The recovered top and a scrying test
lines: Kenzo: Also—what? What’s our anti-scrying technology right now?
Kenzo: We have the top again, don't we?
DM: You do have the top back.
DM: Well, you killed Kadmos, so you could have just taken—you just took it from them.
Delwath: The problem is—wait—the top spins if it’s being—as long as it’s being watched.
DM: Yeah, the problem is the only way you can detect if it—if you’re being scryed is: start it spinning.
DM: And then see whether it falls to the ground or not. See—but here—whether it falls to the ground or not.
Delwath: It takes a few minutes.
Riswynn: We can sporadically check to see if we're being scryed. Even if we are being scryed, we can't do anything about it.

before: DM: I mean, whether they— what their attitudes towards Chardon are, you don’t know. The most prevalent attitude might be, “Don’t care,” right? Like, the further away you get, the more people are just like, “Chardon doesn’t matter to me.”
Kenzo: Right.
DM: “I live in village X,” right? “What matters to me is the politics of village X.”
Kenzo: Cool.
DM: But but not near the canal. The canal is like very centrally part of the Chardonian Empire. You gotta get north as far northwest as you can in order to get away from—
after: Delwath: Well, you can never do anything. I mean, once we get our new room in Vindristjarna, which is scry-proof, then—
Riswynn: Yes.
DM: Right.
Kenzo: I'm feeding you guys steak and cheese from next place.
DM: See you and.

interactions.title: The innkeeper’s advice and a possible pilot
lines: DM: Eventually, it seems like the innkeeper takes pity on you, and you know, comes over and is basically like, “You know, you’re not gonna find a lot of sailors here. Anybody who wasn't pressed into the Navy 2 days ago, probably not somebody you want sailing on your ships anyway, unless you can get one of those halflings to join your crew.”
DM: Yeah, that boat out in the harbor. They don’t usually come this far west. Not sure what—they’re interested in stocking up provisions, not sure where they're sailing to.
Delwath: [garbled] We'll ask a bit more about the navy, right? They're pressing all up and down the coast?
DM: Don't usually go much far west of here. Sailing's a bit tricky until you get to Castrella.
DM: 2 days, if you know the winds and the waters. Maybe less if you’re good. The next big town West.

Delwath: Is there—I’ll ask if there’s any old sailor not healthy enough or able enough to—to be pressed, but who knows the winds in the waters, who might be willing to pilot us to the next town if the halflings won’t help.
DM: Oh, yeah. I can ask around. Not sure anybody will want to go off with a stranger in these trying times, but got someone in mind, actually. Let me think on in a moment.
DM: Really, though, get West, if you're looking for crew, then, something’s in the air, I think. Preparing to blockade the canal or something like that, lot of ships heading in that direction.
DM: Won’t sail much past here for crew, because takes them too much time to get back there. But, right, big trouble.
Delwath: Yeah up. I’ll spend a little bit of time just chatting and trying to get more rumors, right, but not—
DM: You are still in town this evening?
Delwath: Hopefully not. Honestly, we have— we have a a deadline. What’s happening this evening?

DM: Oh, well, you know, Martino might be interested. Piloting— doesn't sail much these days. He hurt his hand fishing accident, 5 years ago now, but to hike up up into the hills to fetch him and think he gets bored, might be interested in your offer.
Delwath: Where up in the hills is he?
DM: Sort of waves his hand up that way, like clearly he lives nearish this. I mean, he's pointing in a direction you could probably find with me.

Delwath: I'm— I will try and get some information so that if I hiked up there myself, I could introduce myself and, like, it wouldn’t be— you know this guy’s name, he’ll tell me where, you know, I could be like, “Such and such sent me,”
Delwath: You know, said you might be interested in a job, blah blah blah. But I wanna go see what the halfling story is first.

before: Delwath: Cast it before it expires, so it—
DM: Right, right.
Delwath: But I don't drop it. And I took Subtle Spell, and nobody will know I'm casting it.
DM: Right.
DM: So yeah, you you you end up recasting it once and and after maybe an hour in town, you’re not—I mean, the inn is quiet. You’re not getting a lot of bites.
after: Delwath: Although now I can’t—I can’t really talk to any of you guys, right? Like, everybody’s telepathy is gone. Yeah. Well—
Riswynn: I—Riswynn was thinking of Sending, since you’ve been gone kind of long.
DM: But okay. So I just—that question should be like—
Riswynn: “How’s it going?”
Delwath: “Halfling boat. What should I ask them?” And—

interactions.title: Pippa welcomes Wellby and offers passage
lines: Wellby: I’ll sort of, like, hail the captain or mate or whoever I can see on deck telepathically, and come out and give him a wave and ask, “Come aboard?”
DM: So you see on deck what seems to be the captain.

DM: She is a sort of stout halfling, wearing a wide-brimmed hat, green—green cloak, like, nice boots, curly brownish hair underneath the hat, smile on her face. Just kind of looking out over the rail, and when she realized you’re a halfling she, like, gives you a big wave, and you can see the ships called the Summer’s Breeze. It seems—the ship seems pretty quiet, actually. Not—
DM: Anyway, she gives you a wave, kind of like signaling, “You coming here? Am I coming there?”
Wellby: I’ll climb aboard, and, like, we’ll tie a little ship against theirs and—
DM: She gives you a little bow with her hat. She introduces herself: “Pippa Greenbarrow at your service.”

Wellby: Wellby Goodbarrel. It is a pleasure. I’m heading around the Cape with my friends here, who have proven to be really deeply incompetent sailors, and looking for a better crew than them. I wonder if there—
DM: Hope they're good at something.
Wellby: Oh, they’re very good at finding treasure and killing the things that have it, which is what we’re about, really.
DM: Sounds like a fun adventure.
Wellby: It—I—I hate— I—I can’t even begin to tell you. I can’t even begin to tell you, so I’m not— W—how about you? Where—where are you bound? Strange things seem afoot in this bay.

DM: Yeah, we're heading up the coast. Not really sure, I guess. I guess probably Castrella is next. From there, we'll see. Might go further north up to Antissus, or somewhere like that. See what, you know, the winds and the feel in the air takes us.
DM: This town is a bit dull. We just stopped, except— well, we needed a few more casks of the ale. What—?
Wellby: What if— what if—and hear me out, cause this is gonna sound like a wild idea for just a minute— what if, instead of going north up the coast, you go west up the coast?
Delwath: North and west, the same direction right here.
Wellby: Admin northeast versus north. What—?
DM: She meant that she was gonna sail up to Castrella and then cut across the— the bay, north up the coast.
DM: Antissus is the next town. It’s like, I don’t know, here or so.

Wellby: Like we're we're looking for some sort of like a mermaid garden in a deep well beyond the point, and we're trying to get there in this thing. And point to a little boat. We could make it worth your while.
DM: Interesting. I can definitely take you as far as Castrella. I guess I just gotta see when you get there. I mean, Roccena's an interesting city. Hmm.
Wellby: Hell of a story! And, you know, the only thing is we’re in a bit of a rush, and I—I don’t know if that works with your schedule.
DM: Well, my crews are all hung over right now.
Wellby: We can probably help with that. We've got some healing among us.

DM: Well, i mean we can go fast if we need to. We don't tend to need to. like I said, we can get you to Castrella if that is— but really, I, you know, can’t promise where we’re gonna go after that till I talk to everybody. I mean, and the—
Wellby: This is fair. And I wouldn’t— I wouldn't presume anything.

Wellby: But what I can say is this: we happen to have— and this is a long way from here, so I don’t know if it’s a thing you’d actually want to do or not, but we've negotiated a trading concession in Ursk. So if you ever wanted to be one of the— how many ships even get into Ursk?— or to trade that in turn with someone who’s on the Green Sea. Clearly we're not going to be doing any trading in Ursk.
DM: You know who would love that? Milo. Wonder where he is these days?
Wellby: I was just gonna say that.
DM: Might be out around Roccena or somewhere like there. He’s often— Last I heard he was trying to sail south of the Sea of Storms. That was a year ago. So either he's dead or he’s made it back.
DM: Tends to avoid the canal. Doesn’t like those creepy windcallers. So if he’s coming up the western coast of the peninsula, maybe we'll find them.
DM: He’s always said if you go far enough east, you can get to the entrance to the Green Sea, sail right around the southern edge of the continent.
DM: Not sure I believe it, but he's come back with some strange stuff.
Wellby: Would be a person who knows how to navigate around the jungles south.
Seeker: Drankor. Yeah, I had him. Interesting point, too.
DM: “Anyway, once my lazy crew”—she stomps on the back of the boat— “rouses themselves from their late night!” She yells down the hatch. “Hey, I’ll take ya. What are you gonna do with your ship?”
Wellby: Oh, we're gonna fold it back into a box again.
DM: Wow! That is something I'd like to see.

before: Delwath: You know, if they’ll—if they’ll come.
DM: Okay, so you're heading up to Martino. The rest of you are sailing. So when you get close, you can see the ship. It’s a— it’s a reasonably—

DM: So you’ve seen a lot of ships like this. It’s sort of similar in design to, like, the Emerald Song or something else that you’ve been on. DM: Looks suspiciously at Delwath as Delwath approaches.
Delwath: I'll shout out.
DM: Who are you?

Delwath: I'm part of a small group where— sailing with some urgency west to custom— what was the name of town? Castrella?

Delwath: Castrella. Well, we hope to go much further, but our chances of augmenting our crew in this this place seem slim at best, so we’ve resolved to do what we can and sail somewhere, get somewhere bigger, so we can hire out some more crew there.
Delwath: But I heard a— from the innkeeper, you might be interested in helping us pilot these waters.
Delwath: Could speed our journey a bit.
DM: Don’t sail much these days. Miss it.
Delwath: How far—how far west do you know the coast?
DM: Oh. Few 100 miles past Castrella.
Delwath: You ever met a mermaid? Merfolk never met him—merfolk.
DM: I have not. Know the songs, though.
Delwath: Do you know the songs?
DM: I don't sing. That’s Chardonian ballad. Don’t quite know what I think of them.
DM: Drag you to the bottom of the ocean and eat you, rescue you from danger.
Delwath: You ever heard of merfolk treasure?
DM: Yeah. Quite a lot. Hunted around these parts.
DM: The collector in Castrella pay good money. Never did find anything to sell.
Delwath: Probably didn't have a map. Delwath’ll then, like, act like he shouldn’t have said that.
Delwath: Shouldn’t have said anything. There’s— can't trust too many people these days.
DM: There’s, like, a twinkle in his eye. “You offering a share of the treasure? Good pilot is hard to find.”
Delwath: I prefer to pay cash. Pay gold. Treasure can be hard to divide.
DM: Well, what are you offering?
Delwath: I'll flash my purse slightly, which is—has a fair bit of gold in it.
Delwath: I'm sure we can come to a fair arrangement. Depends a bit on how far you're willing to come with us, though.
Delwath: At— I'll offer him 25 gold for a week, but can't promise to get you back here.
Delwath: If we abandon you, I could double the offer. Should be able to get back here.
Delwath: 25 gold somewhere safe in Castrella or one of the other villages. We might just have to—
Delwath: Wow, that’s a funny story. At— Darba most recently, but not for some time.
Delwath: No born nearer to the mountains in the east.
DM: Kind of looks— “I don’t know that. Not from the sea, though.”
Delwath: Not from the sea, no. My companions— traveling with a halfling. He knows the sea quite well.
DM: Bow— You should have said from around here.
DM: Sa— way off somewhere east, right?
DM: Well, I don’t think a halfling is gonna leave me stranded somewhere, so, okay, let me pack a bag.
Delwath: Can you meet us down in the— that—coming now? Fine, yeah. Let's go.
Delwath: Meet me—meet me at the inn in an hour. I gotta go—
Delwath: I gotta go hear some songs.

Wellby: It's pretty cool.

interactions.title: The crew wakes and Pippa offers Kenzo a job
lines: Delwath: But that—Delwath swims underwater. You’ve not seen them do this before, deep underwater at the bottom of the water, and come up by the boat right, and climb up into the boat, like, not visible from town, but with, like, gills and fins.
DM: Pippa looks at you a bit strangely. “That’s one of yours?”
Wellby: Delwath, Pippa. Pippa, Delwath. Delwath, real brief, We're gonna sail. They're gonna take us. They're gonna take us. Yeah. I—
Delwath: I hired a guide. Should we bring them?
Wellby: Guess, I say questioningly, looking at Pippa.
Delwath: Plus some songs about merfolk, supposedly. Some guy in town knows it. Thought maybe—we don’t know.
DM: “I don’t think they know any good ones here. We can sing you a song.” Pippa stamps on the that— deck again. “Get up, lazy bones! They want a song.”
Wellby: Have we seen any of the rest of the crew? It’s been like a minute. Like, this is actually a ship crewed by halflings, not, like, zombies or something?

DM: Have not seen any of the rest of the crew, although about 5 min after Wellby looks inquisitively, you can see the first halfling like begin to like, comes up out—out from the lower deck. And, like, it’s a—it’s like a younger woman. Looks probably related to—to Pippa.

DM: She kind of opens her eyes. “Gotta warn us next time. If you want to leave before 2 in the afternoon, gotta go to bed before dawn. Not all of us can go 24 h without sleep like you, Pippa.” She then looks around, like—
Kenzo: I can actually, yeah, I should be able to make them not drunk.
Kenzo: Kenzo comes over and is—gives out knowing, like, not anymore, but I know how—I used to know how you feel. Any gives a—
DM: That's nice. You do that 8 more times.
Kenzo: Why not? I’ll—I’ll use—I’ll use a, like, majority. I’ve never used the majority of my ki to cure, like, a crucial halfling hangover. Pretty very moment.
DM: The rest of the crew basically file up

DM: Everybody, like, coming a little bit—you get the sense it’s not—it’s not entirely that they’re hung over. It’s also, like, they were, like—a good number of them, apparently, were up until 6 or 7 in the morning, and it’s only, like, noon now, so a bit short of sleep.
DM: Looking around hungrily, like, “Better get some food before we sail.” Our whole bunch of chatter, like, “We’re taking all of them? Like, even the weird one with gills?”
DM: Change that back, okay. You know, a bunch of chatter, a bunch of introductions. Like, I’m not gonna introduce the whole crew, but— back—

DM: Summer’s Breeze is clearly a bit of a avenue— not exactly a party boat, but, like, you know, they’re— they’re not—they’re not really caring—they’re not—they’re making money to have fun and not really making money to make money.
DM: Pippa gives a look. Looks over at the crew, all, like, you know, Ready to sail moments after waking up, and then looks over Kenzo and is like—looks at Wellby— “Can I keep him?”
DM: “You want a job?” To Kenzo.
DM: Room and board. As much food as we can cook. Ya. Rare delicacies whenever we come across ’em.
Kenzo: And Kenzo gives a look at Wellby.
Wellby: In fairness, Kenzo that is a much better offer than you currently have.
Riswynn: I mean, Delwath cooks rare delicacies whenever he can find them.

Kenzo: I'll consider it. I'll seriously consider it. How about this? If you don't mind holding that spot for me for like 25, 26 days, that’d be perfect. 26 days, actually. Hold it for 26 days. That’d be perfect.
Kenzo: I just have a feeling that, you know, your offer will be really important, potentially on the 20 fifth day. But, you know, we’ll see what happens.
DM: Hey, you know, you might still be with us in 25 days.
Kenzo: You never know. Never know. Keep that offer open for me, though.

before: Delwath: I'll just work around with all of this.
DM: Doesn’t let— you have to pick one of those things.
Delwath: No, you can change by an action.
DM: Oh, right, right, right, okay.
Delwath: So, so I’ll—when I— when there’s nobody looking, right, I’ll just, like, slip into the water. And then once I’m 3 quarter, you know, once I’m in the water, I’ll turn aquatic, right?
after: DM: So, you ready to go?
Wellby: We pick up the pilot first, and then, yep, head—

DM: Oh yes, the pilot. Let’s— Let's bring them on board. What harm could it do? Aha! Sends a launch out and and as they do, The—you can hear the—the crew down below is prepare—preparing lunch. Beginning— just sing a song. Alice. Oh, yes.
Recorded song: Sailors, brave and true, hoist the sails. When the north winds blow up strong, they sing their songs. A ship sail by.
DM: Oops. Sorry.

Recorded song: These blow up strong, steer clear of the sirens.

Recorded song: Draw you near. Many ships sailed to meet merfolk’s charm, and found all within them dangers hide. Sail high, you near. Brave the waves, but guard your sail, or the merfolk spell will be your jail. A sailor’s tale is old and grand, respect the sea, and he—

Recorded song: I—watch where kelp beds lie, stay clear, as the merfolk draw you near. Brave the waves, but guard your sail, or the merfolk spell be your jail. A sailor’s tale is old and grand, respect the sea and safely land.

DM: And as they finish their song they bring up some food and set lunch for you. And everybody is pretty merry, and they’re clearly intending to eat before they set sail. Well, you’re—well, the poor guy who drew the short straws picking up the pilot.
DM: So by noon, by one or so everybody’s on board. Halflings are introduced. Pippa is introduced to Martino. Martino is impressed that you somehow manage to magically have a halfling ship.

before: Kenzo: I just have a feeling that, you know, your offer will be really important, potentially on the 20 fifth day. But, you know, we’ll see what happens.
DM: Hey, you know, you might still be with us in 25 days.
Kenzo: You never know. Never know. Keep that offer open for me, though.
DM: So, you ready to go?
Wellby: We pick up the pilot first, and then, yep, head—
after: DM: Meanwhile, are you—Delwath is looking like Delwath now?
Delwath: I’m not—yeah. I mean, I’m not gonna keep up the disguise constantly. It's too too difficult.

interactions.title: Martino recognizes Delwath’s disguise and renegotiates
lines: DM: Meanwhile, are you—Delwath is looking like Delwath now?
Delwath: I’m not—yeah. I mean, I’m not gonna keep up the disguise constantly. It's too too difficult.
DM: So Martino looks extremely confused by this whole situation. Looks around, like, “Where’s the guy who hired me?”
Delwath: Delwath will briefly transform back into the guy and explain that there's people after our treasure and an elf's kind of noticeable. I couldn't take chances.
DM: ((Persuasion mechanics)) Definitely looks a bit dubious.

DM: He like like pauses for a while, like clearly weighing in his mind, but also, like, clearly looking at the halfling ship and being like, “I’ve never been on a halfling ship. This must be super interesting.”

DM: And it’s basically like, “This seems dangerous. Got a little extra co—a little extra coin as a insurance against by the risks I’m taking? Looks like you had plenty. Little bit more for a poor old sailor?”
Delwath: I’ll tell him, “Look, I don’t mind paying you a bit more. You’re taking the risks either way, at— if it ends badly, the coin won’t help. Here you go, please,” sort of.
DM: You gotta—you gotta, like—looks at you a bit strangely, like, “Are you trying to convince me to come or not?” Bye—
Delwath: Just being honest with you.
DM: Like, you know, a good handful of gold is pretty life changing for him, so he's doing it.
Delwath: Give them 15, 20 more gold. It's fine.
DM: Sal— you set off sailing on the Summer’s Breeze captained by by Pippa.

DM: Martino really doesn't have much to do. But he’s spending—he’s mostly spending his time just kind of hanging around, like, watching the halflings, just, like, looking, you know, a bit in awe, just clearly happy to be back on a ship sailing into the breeze. He—

DM: And you managed to go— you’re making, you know, 8, 9 miles an hour for for most of the afternoon.
DM: Which is about— which is about 2, while in but 2 hexes.

DM: And you can see here now, you—so you’ve traveled up the coast far enough that you can see there’s, like, a—a gulf or a—a— a bay that cuts in. You can see that on—on Roll20, this, like, thing right here. You’re basically at the mouth of this bay, and there— Castrella is at the far end of this bay. They’re heading— they're heading in.

interactions.title: Tullus sells charts and describes Milo’s ship
lines: DM: Push your way in, in this—this sort of older man, portly man, white hair that’s kind of, like, balding on the top, spectacles, like, down on his nose, right? Like, peering down at something, and hears the bell ring, and he looks up. “Who’s there?”
DM: Pushes up his spectacles. “A little fellow! Yes, come in, come in. Always a pleasure to speak with one of you folk. What—what can I do for you today? Selling or buying?”

Wellby: Well, a little bit of both, maybe trading. I'm looking for maps of the Peninsula, and especially charts of the waters around it. Haven’t been in this direction before, I’d love to understand it better, and I’m helping a group of treasure hunters who, foolish though this may sound, are looking for merfolk. I don't know if merfolk make maps?
DM: No? Well, maybe. I’ve never seen one, but there was a guy in the market who said he was selling merfolk magic. I don’t know, I don’t go in for that sort of thing. Lucas’s name was.
DM: Or, of course, you could talk to Juliana, collects all sorts of merfolk things.
DM: But—but maps! Well, yes, of course, maps of the peninsula. Well, this is a—

DM: ((Map presentation aside)) He pulls out, “Well, this is a— an interesting one, a halfling chart.” And it’s—((Map comparison aside)) like the halfling charts of all these navigation lines drawn all over them that mark currents and things.

DM: Yeah, it’s a— quite a ways out to the— to the tip, to the far end of path— Raziolo, the province. Marks it on the map, like, that’s the province that’s further northwest of where you are now. Like, it’s a whole nother province of the of the Empire.

DM: He’s, like, going on and on, telling you the story of, like, every place as he, like, pushes that map aside and then, like, “Oh, this one better.” This, like, looks off, and in, like, half an hour is gone. And you basically get the sense from him, like, okay, so there’s 3 main provinces on the peninsula:
DM: Portalia, which is where the canal is, like, super Chardonian. Like, that’s where—that’s, like, very closely connected to Chardon itself.

DM: Then there's the hills, that kind of separate Portalia from the the 2 other peninsula provinces. And the other—the Cedrano is where you are now, and then Raziolo is the, like, province at the very far tip.
DM: Cedrano is—is, like, really very coastal, like the hills in the center of the peninsula come almost to the water. I'm—

DM: Raziolo is less so, like, the peninsula, as you go further northwest the hills flattened out, and so there’s roads and, like, interior— make a lot of olive oil there. That's their main export. Main agriculture, the olive trees, some wine. It’s a—that’s the agriculturally rich province. Cedrano’s, like, the fishing province, basically.

DM: Nobody really knows what's around the western side. Like, not that many people go there, but there’s all sorts of stories, and he tells you, like, 15 different stories about merfolk sightings. Like, he has one map he pulls out that’s all the merfolk sightings that are reported, and they’re just, like, random dots everywhere, right? Like, possibly not that helpful.

DM: Talks for a little, you know, just going on and on and on. But you—you get the basic sense from him of this, like, of this sort of layout of— of that, and you pulls out a few more maps. And, you know, it’s like one—one has, like, a bunch of areas west of the peninsula marked with X’s, and these are shipwrecks. People say this is where merfolk drowned the crew, or summoned the fog that made you crash.
DM: I don't know, though. I mean, there’s a lot of shipwrecks, kind of— dangerous when you get out there in the Western Ocean, though.
DM: Gulf of Chardon’s safer. Definitely a lot more shipwrecks around the western side of the peninsula than here.
Wellby: And is there any— Are there any sort of charts of the currents around the western side of the peninsula?
DM: Hmm! You, like, pulls out a few, like, pulls through a bunch of maps.
DM: “Oh, well, not really, actually, the furthest I have a map of is Tamaro Bay.” And he points. That’s, like, a—a bay sort of here, just around the western point.
DM: Yeah, I— do you want it? Yeah, and trade— or— I’ll bock them—sell it to you.
Wellby: A— If I have duplicates of anything that you’d find interesting— I have Eastern Dunmar. I have a portion of the Vermillion Isles.
DM: I don't even know where that is.
Wellby: On the eastern edge of the Green Sea.
DM: Oh, that’s like— That's gotta be a year's sail from here.
Wellby: Oh, at least, I’ve— I don’t know, what are you looking for? I have portions of interior Vostok.
DM: Gotta laugh. I don't know. I mean, I—I’m— mostly do business here, you know.
Wellby: Maybe buying the maps is better than—
DM: Oh, I've got lots of copies of this. I can sell it to you for 10 gold.
Seeker: You're supposed to offer 5. Hello!
DM: Thank you. Lovely doing business with you.
DM: He gives you a little bow. “Tullus is the name. If you ever need more maps—”
DM: Scribe services, charts, I’m here for you.
Wellby: Well, what I really want is the western side of the peninsula, and I don’t—doesn’t sound like that’s gettable.
DM: You know not that many ships go that way. You know who would have a map of that? Been a year since I've seen them.
Wellby: Yep. Been a year since—
DM: And never seen him brave enough or stupid enough to sail down the western coast, but hey, last time he came back with some pretty amazing stuff.
Wellby: What’s the ship look like?
DM: Called the Stormdancer. Bright sails, yellows and blues, triple-masted, big, sturdy ship. Can take— Hmm.
DM: Can handle itself in a gale. Definitely recognize it if you see it.
DM: Massive thundercloud painted on the stern with a laughing face in the middle. Well, good to know.

before: Kenzo: Ken—Kenzo, Kenzo noticed there’s, like, a—there’s, like, some, like, a—basically, like, a kind of, like, a cigarette, or, like, a—like, some tobac—like, a—like, a smoke tobacco thing. And he’s like, “Huh!” He hasn’t, like, you know, done that in a really, really long time. He’s, like, really enjoying his, like, pastry and, like, takes, like, a puff of this, like, tobacco, and then, like, immediately is like, “Oh, fuck, I shouldn’t have done that!” And it’s, like, a little—little, like, woozy, as he’s, like, kind of looking around trying to, you know, make sense of what’s going on around him. It gets like this, like nicotine rush.
DM: Yeah, Kenzo Kenzo is chill, but he's not really picking up much useful information at the moment. Wellby.
Kenzo: By the way, I think Kenzo is very seriously considering this to be, like, hit—like, his—he—he wants—this is—this is a vibe—survive out here. He likes it. He likes it up here.
DM: We cut over to Wellby, who is poking through the market looking for a map seller, right? And, you've got a good nose. Wellby’s got a good nose for these things.

DM: You kind of poke your way around the—the little alleys around the main market, and you can see that you—you find this one shop that— unassuming. There’s, like, only a small sign that has a little scroll on it. But you can see in the, like, one window that is just, like, a messy pile of all sorts of papers and maps and books. This is, like, your—you know, your sort of place.
after: Wellby: Bistlin. Nice Grandpa.

DM: “Okay, my pleasure.” Skipping over to Juliana, after a bit of asking around, you find her—your—her house, and you sort of knock on— on the door, and—and servant comes and lets you in, and and you hear this yelling in in the background like an older woman kind of yelling it in anger at somebody, like, “This is all fraudulent. Never—blacklist him. Never buy anything from that scum Lucas again. None of this is magical at all. Claim merfolk magic. Screw him, he’s never gonna sell anything in this town again.”

DM: And then, like, “Oh, yeah, yeah, show them in,” and you’re led into this study. Quite quite eclectic mix of things. Juliana is a woman in her late fifties. Silver hair, clearly, like, imported Chardonian-style, like, silk robes, elegantly dressed. A couple of silver rings on her fingers, like her hair sort of done up with a—in a bun, sort of tan, blue eyes. Quiet, as you—as you come, and there’s a—a—a younger man who sort of bows and backs out as—as you approach.

DM: She looks up at me, she says, “Welcome!” And you could see, like, scattered around this study there’s, like, probably a hundred different little trinkets of various kinds, like some made of coral, some made of shell, all something, like, ocean-related.
DM: What is—what was your story? Your—your treasure hunters making contact because you are hoping to have something to sell?

interactions.title: Juliana shows merfolk craft and discusses its dangers
lines: DM: “Okay, my pleasure.” Skipping over to Juliana, after a bit of asking around, you find her—your—her house, and you sort of knock on— on the door, and—and servant comes and lets you in, and and you hear this yelling in in the background like an older woman kind of yelling it in anger at somebody, like, “This is all fraudulent. Never—blacklist him. Never buy anything from that scum Lucas again. None of this is magical at all. Claim merfolk magic. Screw him, he’s never gonna sell anything in this town again.”

DM: And then, like, “Oh, yeah, yeah, show them in,” and you’re led into this study. Quite quite eclectic mix of things. Juliana is a woman in her late fifties. Silver hair, clearly, like, imported Chardonian-style, like, silk robes, elegantly dressed. A couple of silver rings on her fingers, like her hair sort of done up with a—in a bun, sort of tan, blue eyes. Quiet, as you—as you come, and there’s a—a—a younger man who sort of bows and backs out as—as you approach.

DM: She looks up at me, she says, “Welcome!” And you could see, like, scattered around this study there’s, like, probably a hundred different little trinkets of various kinds, like some made of coral, some made of shell, all something, like, ocean-related.
((Repeated setup, private discussion and persuasion mechanics))
Seeker: We're a— we’re interested in the real thing. We’ve—we’ve heard that that’s what you deal in.
DM: I will pay good money for genuine merfolk artifacts, indeed, yes. So much schlock these days gets passed off as merfolk craft. All fake.
DM: Oh, it's obvious if you look carefully enough. “Look at this.” She holds up, like, a—like, a spiral sort of coral pendant that’s hanging on necklace.
DM: “Clearly not genuine merfolk work. I mean, first of all, what is this? They never make necklaces. That’s not their jewelry. That’s pathetic and pointless.” She, like, just crushes it.
DM: “And if this were magical, I would not be able to crush it in my hand.” She throws it on the ground. “Scammers. Pathetic.”
Seeker: Seeker strolls over to the cabinets on the wall, holding interesting objects, and peers in to find one that catches his eye.
DM: The first thing that catches eye is— it almost looks like— it’s—it’s a sphere.

DM: It almost looks like— like, if you, like, you could twist it and there’s, like—it’s like a mechanical something that would spin if you just twist it in the right way. There’s, like, a latch and, like, a—a gear, almost like the— like a kind of like a spherical music box of some kind, but clearly with some mechanical complexity to it. Completely blue.
DM: Hard to tell. It's in a glass cabinet.
Seeker: I look over. But may I?
DM: “Back, back, back!” She comes out from behind her desk. “Step back, please.” Was very Gallic.
DM: She’s clearly in a bad mood. She reaches, she opens the cabinet, puts on this white glove, and reaches and—and lifts out this blue thing in the hand of the glove, made—
DM: “Don’t rightly know what this is, in fact.”

DM: But—and she’s, like, she’s wearing gloves on both hands. She, like, pokes it very gently, and it ripples almost as if it’s made of water and then goes still again. She holds it really gently, and she starts to twist it a little bit. Now she twists, you can see that there's it’s actually not—like, it looks mechanical, but it’s not, because it turns entirely fluid as she begins to twist it, and this, like, this watery design begins to spout up and flow into these sort of— yeah, like, like, sort of twirling sort of confetti or something like that.
DM: The real trick: if you put it in seawater turns solid. Hmm! Don’t know what it is. This is genuine merfolk magic.
DM: Carefully puts it back. Takes the gloves off.
DM: “And you are selling things? Hope to sell things?”
DM: Trust you are more genuine seekers of artifacts than the fools and sycophants who sell in the markets in this town these days.
Seeker: We are experienced collectors ourselves. A— Perhaps we could make an arrangement.
DM: Do not buy sight unseen.
Seeker: No, but we’re new to the area, so if you have some way to point us in the right direction, we might assure you that we won't deal with any other collector.
DM: You’re treasure hunters, but you don’t know where to look? Wretch—
((Repeated setup, private discussion and persuasion mechanics))
DM: I love that. “Aspiring treasure hunter, one might say. Well, you have something to sell, come back and I’ll look at it.”
Delwath: It's not that we don’t know where to look exactly, that—them— path is tricky to follow.
Delwath: And we're seeking those who might share what they know so that we can try and piece the pieces together.
Delwath: We've found plenty of treasures. We are not new at this game.
Delwath: I could show you some if it would help convince you. They’re not merfolk treasures, though. Dragon hoard.
DM: Yes, I mean, the amount of magic you carry as if it’s nothing. Clearly you have found treasures, not doubting that, but— so merfolk treasures are different. G—
DM: Have you— Have you spent days beneath the sea? Can you breathe water? Can you—?
((Repeated setup, private discussion and persuasion mechanics))
DM: Well, perhaps you have some thinking to do about your approach.
((Repeated setup, private discussion and persuasion mechanics))

DM: She kind of looks, “I don’t really know what you’re asking. You want me to just tell you stuff? Yeah, you have nothing to sell, nothing to trade. Very happy to buy from you, should you show up back at my house with genuine merfolk treasure.”
Delwath: I was given to understand you are quite committed to your collecting.
Delwath: And we are trying to unravel a puzzle which I cannot share too much about.
Delwath: But we are here offering something in trade. What we’re offering in trade is your right of first refusal for the treasures of the merfolk that we find.
Seeker: That's what I was trying to say before.
Delwath: May not be worth anything to you, but I think, looking at us, you are aware that at— we have succeeded at these quests in the past. We expect to have something to trade ends—
Delwath: Frankly, you don’t seem like the easiest person to work with, so you shouldn’t expect necessarily that you will be our first port of call.
Delwath: But we're here to negotiate and make a deal mutually beneficial one.
Delwath: You get an opportunity to buy something new. We get an opportunity to sell something.

Delwath: What we're asking for is—and I apologize for being so cryptic— at— whatever you can tell us about prior successes that people have had, or whatever you can tell us about where the kelp grows.
((Repeated setup, private discussion and persuasion mechanics))
DM: Okay. I mean, she looks a little bit, like, put off by you calling her rude and a bit, like, a little bit annoyed, just, like—
DM: But she’s like, “Look, I— the truth is, I'm skeptical because it's been more 20 years now—more than 20 years— since anybody has credibly visited the merfolk and returned.”
Seeker: So where did all these artifacts come from?
DM: Well, I bought up a lot of things that have been circulating for some time. Every now and then people find things washed up on the beach during shipwrecks.
Delwath: Wait a minute, when did the jade hand fragment—?
DM: At about 30 years ago. And there’s a lot of fakes.
Seeker: So you're saying a new cache of authentic goods could be of very high value?
DM: Could. But you are not the first to try.
Seeker: Naturally, as time grows on, and the stakes increase.
DM: With a rare few exceptions, it's been a long time since anybody sailed around the point and returned.
DM: There’s something out there in the Endless Ocean, and for all your obvious magic, forgive me if I am not totally convinced that you too will return.
DM: But none have before— a— wow— almost none.
DM: Milo Thistlefoot managed to sail that way, but he’s been missing for a year now, so—
Seeker: Who was the last to come back 20 years ago?
DM: Oh, I don’t know, I—I don’t remember. I mean, didn’t used to be that rare for people—people would fish off there.
DM: I don't know who was the last to come back. Yeah, hmm. But it’s been a while.
Seeker: There anything you can reveal to us about your buyers, who’s interested in this stuff that you deal with?
DM: Oh, I don't sell. I collect.
Seeker: Oh, you’re just— a— but—and, forgive me for my ignorance of how to run the numbers here, but it seems like you’d have a cash flow problem then.
DM: My wealth does not come from my collection. My wealth enables my collection.
Seeker: I see. And might one— may ask its origin? O—
DM: That is a boring story.
Seeker: Well, and we'll skip right over you.
((Repeated setup, private discussion and persuasion mechanics))
Delwath: I was gonna ask her if she knew where the Elemental Sea is.
DM: There are many who say that if you swim deep enough, the right part of the Endless Ocean, you can swim to another plane. Is that what you mean?
Delwath: Just a word I heard once.
DM: Not heard that exact turn of phrase. Elemental Ocean?
DM: I mean, there are many stories, there’s folk tales. I don’t think any of them are true.
DM: Not bothered much with what the fisher folk sing of the mermaids and the merfolk.
DM: Seems all too disconnected from hard truth that you can hold in your hand.
DM: Well, maybe you do know something. I'll be impressed if you return with anything to sell.
Delwath: Do you know Milo, or do you know Milo relatively well?
DM: Everybody knows Milo, and nobody knows Milo.
Delwath: Do you know of—are there any ports—portraits of him in town? O—
Delwath: Well enough to draw likeness.
DM: I mean, you could ask the halflings. There's a bunch of them around. Think a ship came into port this morning— Breeze, something breezy, wind.
Delwath: Oh, they probably know him well enough to—

before: Wellby: What’s the ship look like?
DM: Called the Stormdancer. Bright sails, yellows and blues, triple-masted, big, sturdy ship. Can take— Hmm.
DM: Can handle itself in a gale. Definitely recognize it if you see it.
DM: Massive thundercloud painted on the stern with a laughing face in the middle. Well, good to know.
Wellby: Bistlin. Nice Grandpa.
after: DM: We can come back if there’s anything else you wanna say. But skipping over to Riswynn for a minute, so, wandering through town, looking for—just, like, trying to get a sense of the place and—and looking, you don’t—you don’t get the sense that this is a heavily sort of craft-oriented city, right? I mean, obviously there’s, like, a handful of—I mean, there’s some blacksmith. There’s—there’s barrelwrights and things, but it’s not the sort of place that has a huge— I'll be—
Riswynn: Roughly.
DM: You know, crafting district or something like that. Like,

DM: You know, there’s the—the sort of heart of the city has, like—trade seems to be its main wealth, right? Like, there’s merchant houses, there’s— I mean, you see, like big barrels of olive oil being rolled into warehouses, and me— you know, wine and and cheese and salted fish, lots of salted fish.

DM: And there's like, there's basically no dwarves like this entire—like, both in this city and in the smaller village, you haven’t seen any dwarves, which is a little unusual, but maybe not super unexpected, given how far you are away from, like, the known dwarven centers of— and most dwarves aren’t super thrilled about boats. Damn!

interactions.title: An image-assisted scry of Milo fails
lines: Kenzo: Let’s get a picture, Mi—Milo, scry him.
DM: The scry does not work.
Seeker: Did we get an an image of him, or was that without it? No, that’s—
Delwath: An image. That’s with an image.
DM: Can try again tomorrow, once every 24 h. But— Spain—

before: DM: You could. Yeah, you could certainly try. That might end poorly, but—
Seeker: Definitely would.
DM: I—I mean, there are spells that—that are for 24 h. You just would need to find somebody who could cast one.
Seeker: Great. Me—
DM: So, okay. What does—what do you all—what does everybody want to do?
after: Riswynn: How long is the sail up there? Assuming we convince the halflings to take us there.
Delwath: I mean, if we can’t convince that one to take us there, the next step—we also need to hire sailors here and—
DM: So it’s—yeah, it’s like 360 miles.
Kenzo: 2.
DM: So if we could go 24 h—

interactions.title: Rumors of Dorian and Kazuro
lines: DM: But it’s been 20, 25 years or something like that since anything’s happened. However, there is this supposed guy, Dorian something or other, that you keep hearing his name brought up that— like, asking about who’s been to visit the merfolk, nobody's seen him for like 20 years, but he claimed he was obsessed with the merfolk.
DM: He used to live in Castrella. He left— He left 25 years ago to go find the merfolk.
DM: And there’s—there’s rumors, like, of this guy, the Mystic of Tamaro Bay. Some people think that is him, supposedly can breathe water.
Kenzo: But he left 25 years ago?
DM: He left 25 years ago. Like, there’s these rumors, like, there’s this weird guy, like— Tamaro Bay is, like, as far west as anybody sails.

DM: So is it the same guy? Like, there’s—you get the sense this is, like, a local conspiracy theory, like, Dorian— Dorian Almare, who was obsessed with merfolk, is now the Mystic of Tamaro Bay and learned how to breathe underwater. Whether it’s true or not, like, nobody really knows. We found it—
Kenzo: Out in the ocean, in the west.
Kenzo: Allegedly where in the ocean, in the west? He, like, went west and disappeared?
DM: He went west and disappeared, like, on the coast. So Tamaro Bay is what—is, like, right on the coast, just around the tip of the peninsula.

DM: The other bit of information you hear again is like, “Oh, you should—” asking about merfolk—“Oh, you should— there’s all these folk songs, you should go ask, and that—you should go listen in the inns. But also, you’re trying to breathe underwater, Kazuro is who you should look for.”

DM: He’s a stoneborn hermit guy. He lives in a cave somewhere up the coast. Nobody really quite knows where, but he's supposed to be an expert in like potions and alchemy, and has the tricks for brewing a magic that lets you breathe the water.
